message.content: The kernel uses the Abramowitz–Stegun erfc approximation, whose probability error (~1.5e-7) gets multiplied by |x| in GELU, so the 1e-6 absolute tolerance may be violated for |x| in the ~4–27 range. The contract explicitly requires the tolerance over every finite FP16 value, so I'll probe the entire domain exhaustively.

function.arguments: {"rationale": "The A&S 26.2.17-style rational tail approximation has Phi-approximation error up to ~1.5e-7, and GELU error scales as |x|*|Phi_err|, which likely exceeds 1e-6 for |x| of order 5-27 where the exp envelope hasn't underflowed and erfc is still non-negligible.", "scope": "in_scope", "scope_evidence": [{"source": "problem.txt", "summary": "'EVERY finite FP16 value is legal, including both signed zeros, positive and negative subnormal values, and both extrema +/-65504' and 'Every output element must satisfy abs(actual[i] - GELU(x[i])) <= 1e-6 ... throughout the entire legal domain.'"}], "scope_rationale": "The contract requires abs(actual - GELU(x)) <= 1e-6 for every finite FP16 input, so a violation anywhere in that enumerated domain breaks the contract.", "statement": "The kernel's Abramowitz-Stegun tail approximation produces GELU error exceeding the contract's 1e-6 absolute tolerance for some finite FP16 input value."}

message.reasoning_content:
The kernel uses A&S 26.2.17 erfc approximation, max abs error ~1e-7 on erfc, but probability error can be up to ~2e-7? Actually A&S 7.1.26 error < 1.5e-7 for erfc... but GELU tolerance is 1e-6 absolute on output. GELU(x)=x*Phi, error = |x|*|Phi_err| ≤ 65504 * 1.5e-7 ≈ 0.01 — fails for large x. But for large |x|, GELU(x) ≈ x for positive x and ≈ 0 for negative, so absolute error of GELU itself isn't amplified that way. Actually GELU error = x * Phi_err(x). For large positive x, Phi ≈1, err in Phi ~1.5e-7 → x*1.5e-7; x=65504 → ~0.0098 > 1e-6. Also envelope underflow: exp(-x²/2) underflows for x>~27 (exp(-365) subnormal/zero at ~x=27 in fp32: exp(-887) =0). So for x ≥ ~27, tail=0, probability=1 (positive) → GELU=x, error = x*(1-Phi(x)) which is tiny for x>27? 1-Phi(27) ~ 1e-160, fine. For x in some mid range where approximation error matters: x~5-10: x*|Phi_err|. A&S 26.2.17 error |eps| ≤ 1.5e-7, so 10*1.5e-7=1.5e-6 > 1e-6 potentially. But coefficients here are truncated (1.06141, -1.45315, 1.42141, -0.28450, 0.25483) — the standard A&S values. Also note the polynomial sign pattern: A&S P(t)=1.061405429 t^5 -1.453152027 t^4 +1.421413741 t^3 -0.284496736 t^2 +0.254829592 t. Same. So err ~1.5e-7 in Phi, GELU err = x*err, up to 1.5e-6 for x~10? But actual error distribution: error term changes sign; max might exceed 1e-6 for some x in 1-27 range. Worth probing: sweep all FP16 values, compare to FP64 erfc reference, check max abs error.

Also note kernel validates finite, contract allows all finite FP16 — good. Contiguous views with nonzero offsets: kernel loads X+index from data pointer — Triton passes data_ptr() which includes offset, fine. Subnormals fine. Signed zeros: x<0.0 false for -0.0? -0.0 < 0.0 is false → probability=1-tail; tail computed with magnitude 0: t=1, poly=... compute: t=1: 1.06141-1.45315+1.42141-0.2845+0.25483 = 0.0? sum: 1.06141-1.45315=-0.39174; +1.42141=1.02967; -0.2845=0.74517; +0.25483=1.0. So poly*envelope=1, tail=0.5, prob = 1-0.5=0.5 for +0 and -0? For -0: x<0.0 false in IEEE (-0==0), so prob=0.5, value=-0*0.5=-0.0. Reference: 0.5*(-0)*erfc(0)= -0. Signed zeros equivalent. OK.

Record claim: approximation error exceeds 1e-6 somewhere in legal domain. Probe: enumerate all 65536 fp16 finite values (excluding NaN/inf), compute kernel output and FP64 reference, max abs diff. That's the decisive probe.
